_doc: Allowlist of KNOWN differences between the committed golden manifests and the WXT-generated ones, consumed by scripts/parity-harness.mjs.
Every entry names the phase that retires it. The harness fails on any diff NOT listed here AND on any entry that no longer occurs — this file only shrinks.
diffs[].path uses the harness's /key/subkey notation; arrays diff as one unit at their own path.
missingReferences[] are manifest-referenced files a stub build does not carry yet.
Red-proofed 2026-08-12: removing a live entry AND adding a stale one each failed the harness (exit 1).

P1 retired (2026-08-12, real entrypoints landed): /icons, /action/default_icon (explicit ICONS in wxt.config match the goldens exactly), the assets/* and index.html missingReferences (public/ carries the shipped set; the WAR names popup.html).
golden-rebaseline entries are structural renames the bundled build cannot avoid; they retire when the goldens are re-frozen from the shipped 1.4.0 manifests.

diffs.reason: WXT derives default_title from the popup <title>; harmless addition the shipped 1.3.1 manifest does not have. Relabelled 2026-08-13: P2 shipped without adopting it, and back-dating a frozen 1.3.1 snapshot would falsify the golden — it retires when the goldens are re-frozen from 1.4.0
WXT names the popup page popup.html (renamed in P1 — background.js mints the same URL, pinned in tests/background-caller-relay.test.mjs); golden still says index.html until re-frozen

the 11-file classic-script js list became one bundle (content-scripts/content.js) and the css re-attached at its bundled path — entrypoints/content.ts owns the effect order; 1.4.15 adds the porkbun.com/checkout/* MAIN-world document_start alert-shim entry (content-scripts/porkbun-alert.js), same on Chrome and Firefox
the WAR page renamed index.html → popup.html with the popup entrypoint (P1); assets/* unchanged

Mozilla data-collection consent declaration added 2026-08-13 (mandatory for AMO; audit-backed mapping in wxt.config.ts) — the 1.3.1 golden predates the framework

1.4.5 -> 1.4.28 (package.json is the single version authority): first-install welcome page (background.js runtime.onInstalled opens /welcome on reason install) for install attribution (1.4.6), every toolbar and store icon is the site favicon mark again, the white italic C on the orange rounded square, replacing the 1.4.5 header wordmark that was unreadable at icon size (1.4.7), and checkout code sharing is opt-in behind an explicit in-extension consent prompt (1.4.8), and the checkout submission carries that consent as proof for the server gate (1.4.9), and the Safari build carries a 40-character manifest name for App Store Connect (1.4.10; the Chrome and Firefox manifests are unchanged), and the popup's 'Did it work?' vote plus per-shopper hide controls (1.4.11; popup UI only, the manifests are unchanged), and capture of a shopper-typed code is armed on the page load that resumes a pending auto-apply submit (1.4.12; content script only, the manifests are unchanged), and the promo-box finder, the server-picked coupon box and the input-only pick that applies on Enter (1.4.13; content script and background only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and the opt-in anonymous code-sharing funnel diagnostics (1.4.14; content script, background and popup only, no permission or host_permission change; the Firefox manifest gains only the optional technicalAndInteraction data-collection entry, inside the already-allowlisted data_collection_permissions path, and the Chrome manifest is unchanged), and the porkbun.com checkout alert shim, a MAIN-world document_start content script that turns the native coupon-failure alert() into a DOM marker so the apply run does not freeze, plus the alert-shim capability proof the server gates porkbun.com's apply config on, the per-device telemetry-id wording and no reuse of a telemetry id after a failed delete, and Safari signing in through the website like Firefox (1.4.15; no permission or host_permission change, host_permissions is already https://*/*; the Chrome and Firefox manifests each gain only one content_scripts entry, matches https://porkbun.com/checkout/*, js content-scripts/porkbun-alert.js, run_at document_start, world MAIN, inside the already-allowlisted /content_scripts path), and the Safari every-site permission banner that no longer claims Caramel cannot run on every store, an Enable button that works and Apple buttons that recover, with iPhone and iPad steps that name the page menu and Always Allow on Every Website, plus the coupon card 'New customers only' label (1.4.16; popup and permission-state.js only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and the code-capture refusal reasons plus the toolbar badge no longer bursting the shared rate limit (1.4.17; content script and background only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and the coupon box found and proved on a store with no config, saved as that store's config, with the finder and the apply flow behind it hardened, removing our coupon never clicking a product line's remove, and the toolbar and store icons recreated from the vector master (1.4.18; content script and background only, the finder and selector builders ship as on-demand files under the already web-accessible assets/*, no permission or host_permission change, the icon paths are unchanged, the manifests are unchanged), and auto-detect hardened across store kinds: a found box's parts named by their hook class, a total the store re-draws read again, a saved box's answer read like a found box's, store refusals read from page alerts and quoted in whole words, totals and prices read in more languages, currencies and number formats (Indian lakh, Swiss), and Shopify's discount-or-gift-card box watched for auto-save (1.4.19; content script, background and popup only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and the apply run always tries its first three codes before the time budget can stop it, with the savings card never coming up over the prompt pill (1.4.20; content script only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and an apply run that stops waiting as soon as a store repeats its last refusal, and that carries on across a store whose coupon POST lands after the attempt stopped waiting and across a browser slow to answer extension storage between reloads (1.4.21; content script only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and an apply run that tries the next code when the store accepts one that takes nothing off, with a progress count that carries on across reloads (1.4.22; content script only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and a store whose configured promo-box toggle or apply button went stale is still reached through the box's own collapsible header and its form's one button (1.4.23; content script only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and a code the store refuses as a "NOT APPLIED" row is read as its answer and taken off before the next code (1.4.24; content script only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and a cart that asks "remove this coupon?" has its dialog confirmed after its fade-in, so a refused code really comes off (1.4.25; content script only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and the Caramel logo keeps its small size when the UI stylesheet is slow to load, so the savings card stays readable (1.4.26; content script only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and the final card quoting a store refusal without a coupon row's close glyph, a browser with no chromiumapp.org redirect signing in through the website, and a box the finder picked waiting for a Shopify discount that lands seconds after the total re-draws with the same number (1.4.27; content script and popup only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged), and the supported-store cache kept packed so Safari's storage quota accepts it, a finder flag question that is always answered and falls back on the last known flag, and the earlier code credited when the next is refused for existing discounts (1.4.28; content script and background only, no permission or host_permission change, the manifests are unchanged). The goldens are frozen 1.3.1 snapshots relabelled 1.4.0 and cannot follow a release without being re-frozen

runtime-requestable every-website grant, added 2026-08-19 so permission-state.js requestAllSites() can ask for it from a click (see the wxt.config.ts note); a no-op on Chrome, declared for all browsers to keep one code path

runtime-requestable every-website grant, added 2026-08-19 so permission-state.js requestAllSites() can ask for it from a click; the Gecko contract is that request() may only name origins the manifest listed as optional, and the Firefox <=1.0.3 upgrade cohort is exactly who needs to ask

Firefox for Android availability (issue #218): AMO derives a version's Android compatibility from this key — the live 1.4.1 listing carries no android entry, so the extension was never offered on Firefox for Android. strict_min_version 120.0 = the first Android Firefox with the open extension ecosystem
the env stamp is BUNDLED into background.js instead of a separate manifest entry — the stamp-first guarantee moves from manifest order into the module graph (P1 pins it there)
